To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temporal anticipation of upcoming sensations is mediated by the hippocampus and that the temporal anticipation for upcoming actions is mediated by the cerebellum.

1) the temporal anticipation of an action is associated with increased activity in a specific brain area, the cerebellum, 2) this anticipation is not associated with activity in a different brain area, the basal ganglia, and 3) the temporal anticipation that occurs when a person is waiting for an action to be performed is associated with increased basal ganglia activity, but not with cerebellar activity

(1) the ability to anticipate the timing and occurrence of future events is critical for the successful execution of goal-directed behavior; (2) temporal anticipation can occur in two distinct forms; (3) these two forms are associated with different neural mechanisms; and (4) the two forms of temporal anticipation are differentially recruited depending on the goal of the behavior

how the brain represents time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain uses a variety of different mechanisms to anticipate time in a variety of different ways for a variety of different purposes.
the human brain uses two distinct neural mechanisms to predict the timing of upcoming events.
the neural basis for temporal anticipation depends on the type of temporal regularity, on whether it is a sensory or a motor regularity, and on the goal of the anticipation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal anticipation is a complex phenomenon, and the brain uses different neural mechanisms for different purposes.
we are not only interested in how the brain anticipates the future but also how this ability is used to guide behavior.
the brain uses different strategies to anticipate the timing and duration of upcoming events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain uses two distinct mechanisms to anticipate the timing when we need to act and when we need to perceive.
temporal anticipation can serve a variety of goals and that these goals are reflected in the neural mechanisms that implement anticipation.
temporal anticipation is not a monolithic process.
